approvalTitle: Tasks Document - Coffee Evaluation Implementation Tasks
content:
# Tasks Document - Coffee Evaluation Feature

## Phase 1: Database & API Layer

- [ ] 1.1. Run database migrations
  - File: supabase/migrations/20251231010000_coffee_evaluations_schema.sql
  - Execute migration to create coffee_evaluations and user_profiles tables
  - Verify RLS policies and indexes are created
  - Purpose: Set up database schema with proper security and performance
  - _Leverage: Existing migration file created by supabase-db-designer_
  - _Requirements: All (database foundation)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Database Administrator with Supabase expertise | Task: Execute the database migration file to create coffee_evaluations and user_profiles tables with RLS policies and indexes, verifying all constraints and triggers are properly set up | Restrictions: Do not modify existing auth.users table, ensure RLS is enabled before creating policies, verify pg_trgm extension is available | Success: All tables created with proper structure, RLS policies active and tested, indexes created for performance, triggers functioning correctly_

- [ ] 1.2. Create TypeScript types for coffee evaluation
  - File: lib/types/coffee.ts
  - Define CoffeeEvaluation and UserProfile interfaces matching database schema
  - Add validation types for form inputs
  - Purpose: Establish type safety for coffee evaluation data structures
  - _Leverage: Database schema from design.md, existing type patterns_
  - _Requirements: 1, 2, 3 (data structure for all CRUD operations)_
  - _Prompt: Role: TypeScript Developer specializing in type systems and database schema mapping | Task: Create comprehensive TypeScript interfaces for CoffeeEvaluation and UserProfile matching the PostgreSQL schema, including validation types for form inputs with proper null handling and date string types | Restrictions: Match database schema exactly (nullable fields must be type | null), use ISO string for timestamps, include validation helper types, follow existing type naming conventions | Success: All interfaces compile without errors, proper null/undefined handling, types match database schema precisely, includes helper types for form validation_

- [ ] 1.3. Implement data fetching layer (lib/api/coffee.ts)
  - File: lib/api/coffee.ts
  - Create cached data fetching functions using React cache()
  - Implement getCoffeeEvaluations, getCoffeeEvaluation, searchCoffeeEvaluations
  - Purpose: Provide memoized data access layer for Server Components
  - _Leverage: lib/supabase/server.ts, React cache() pattern, existing API patterns_
  - _Requirements: 2 (list view), 3 (detail view), 6 (search)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Backend Developer with Next.js App Router and Supabase expertise | Task: Implement data fetching layer with React cache() wrapper following Next.js Best Practices patterns, creating functions for list/detail/search operations using Supabase client from lib/supabase/server.ts | Restrictions: Must use React cache() for request memoization, handle Supabase errors gracefully, return properly typed data, do not expose raw Supabase queries to components | Success: All fetch functions properly cached, error handling robust, TypeScript types correct, Server Components can use these functions without duplication_

- [ ] 1.4. Implement Server Actions (lib/actions/coffee.ts)
  - File: lib/actions/coffee.ts
  - Create Server Actions for CRUD operations
  - Implement createCoffeeEvaluation, updateCoffeeEvaluation, deleteCoffeeEvaluation
  - Add revalidatePath and redirect logic
  - Purpose: Provide type-safe mutation layer with automatic CSRF protection
  - _Leverage: lib/supabase/server.ts, Next.js redirect/revalidatePath, existing action patterns_
  - _Requirements: 1 (create), 4 (edit), 5 (delete)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Full-stack Developer with Next.js Server Actions expertise | Task: Implement Server Actions for CRUD operations using FormData, with proper error handling, revalidatePath for cache invalidation, and redirect for navigation following Next.js Best Practices | Restrictions: Must use 'use server' directive, validate all inputs, handle Supabase errors with user-friendly messages, use revalidatePath before redirect, return {error: string} for client-side error display | Success: All CRUD operations work correctly, form submissions handled properly, errors returned to client gracefully, cache invalidation and navigation work as expected_

## Phase 2: Core UI Components

- [ ] 2.1. Create CoffeeSlider component
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/shared/coffee-slider.tsx
  - Implement custom slider with 1-10 range and coffee theme styling
  - Add accessibility features (keyboard navigation, aria attributes)
  - Purpose: Provide reusable slider component for rating inputs
  - _Leverage: Frontend-design plugin output (coffee-slider CSS), Tailwind config_
  - _Requirements: 1 (evaluation creation with slider inputs)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Frontend Developer specializing in accessible React components and Tailwind CSS | Task: Create a fully accessible slider component (1-10 range) with coffee theme styling from frontend-design output, supporting keyboard navigation (arrow keys), touch gestures, and proper ARIA attributes | Restrictions: Must be a Client Component ('use client'), follow frontend-design styling exactly, ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, handle controlled component pattern correctly | Success: Slider is fully accessible and keyboard-navigable, matches design exactly, works on touch devices, emits onChange events properly_

- [ ] 2.2. Create RatingStars component
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/shared/rating-stars.tsx
  - Implement star rating display with partial fill support
  - Add size variants (sm, md, lg)
  - Purpose: Provide visual rating display for evaluation cards and details
  - _Leverage: Frontend-design plugin output (rating stars), Tailwind utilities_
  - _Requirements: 2 (list view card display), 3 (detail view display)_
  - _Prompt: Role: UI Developer with expertise in SVG icons and React components | Task: Create a presentational RatingStars component supporting 1-10 rating scale (converted to 5 stars with half-star precision), with size variants following frontend-design output styling using Tailwind CSS | Restrictions: Must be a presentational component (no state), use inline SVG for stars, support partial fills accurately (e.g., 7/10 = 3.5 stars), optimize for performance with React.memo if needed | Success: Stars render correctly for all rating values, partial fills work precisely, size variants apply correctly, component is lightweight and performant_

- [ ] 2.3. Create CoffeeCard component
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/list/card.tsx
  - Implement evaluation card with coffee theme styling
  - Add hover effects and animations
  - Include shop name, bean type, overall rating, and date
  - Purpose: Display individual evaluation in list view
  - _Leverage: Frontend-design plugin output (CoffeeCard), RatingStars component, Next.js Link_
  - _Requirements: 2 (list view card display)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Frontend Developer with expertise in card-based UI and Tailwind animations | Task: Create CoffeeCard component following frontend-design output exactly, including hover effects (translateY, shadow), gold accent overlay, and responsive design using RatingStars for rating display and Next.js Link for navigation | Restrictions: Must match frontend-design styling precisely, use Next.js Link for client-side navigation, ensure accessibility with proper semantic HTML, optimize for grid layouts (1/2/3 columns) | Success: Cards match design exactly, hover effects smooth and performant, clickable area works correctly, accessible with keyboard navigation, responsive across all breakpoints_

## Phase 3: List & Detail Pages

- [ ] 3.1. Create list page container (Server Component)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_containers/list/container.tsx
  - Implement Server Component for data fetching
  - Use getCoffeeEvaluations from lib/api/coffee.ts
  - Purpose: Fetch and pass data to presentational view component
  - _Leverage: lib/api/coffee.ts (cached fetch), Container/Presentational pattern_
  - _Requirements: 2 (list view)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Next.js Developer with Server Components expertise | Task: Create a Server Component container that fetches evaluations using getCoffeeEvaluations from lib/api/coffee.ts and passes data to CoffeeListView, following Container/Presentational pattern from structure.md | Restrictions: Must be a Server Component (no 'use client'), use async/await for data fetching, handle errors with error.tsx boundary, do not include UI logic in container | Success: Container fetches data correctly using cached function, passes properly typed data to view, errors are caught by error boundary, Server Component optimization works as expected_

- [ ] 3.2. Create list page view (Presentational Component)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/list/view.tsx
  - Implement list display with responsive grid (1/2/3 columns)
  - Show empty state when no evaluations
  - Purpose: Display list of coffee evaluations in grid layout
  - _Leverage: CoffeeCard component, Tailwind grid utilities_
  - _Requirements: 2 (list view with responsive grid)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Frontend Developer specializing in responsive layouts and React patterns | Task: Create CoffeeListView presentational component that renders evaluations in responsive grid (mobile: 1 col, tablet: 2 col, desktop: 3 col) using CoffeeCard, with empty state message and "Create" link when no data | Restrictions: Must be a Server Component (receives server data), use Tailwind responsive utilities (sm:, md:, lg:), implement proper empty state UX, maintain grid layout consistency | Success: Grid responds correctly across breakpoints, empty state shows helpful message with action link, all evaluations render as cards, layout is consistent and visually appealing_

- [ ] 3.3. Create main list page (Composition Root)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/page.tsx
  - Compose container and view components
  - Add page metadata for SEO
  - Purpose: Main entry point for coffee evaluations list
  - _Leverage: CoffeeListContainer, Next.js metadata API_
  - _Requirements: 2 (list view)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Next.js Developer with App Router expertise | Task: Create main coffee list page that renders CoffeeListContainer, exports metadata for SEO (title, description in Japanese), and serves as composition root following Next.js App Router patterns | Restrictions: Must be a Server Component, export proper metadata object, minimal logic (composition only), use Suspense if needed for loading states | Success: Page renders correctly with proper metadata, composition pattern clean and maintainable, SEO optimized with Japanese metadata_

- [ ] 3.4. Create detail page container (Server Component)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/[id]/_containers/evaluation/container.tsx
  - Fetch single evaluation by ID
  - Handle not found and authorization errors
  - Purpose: Fetch evaluation data for detail view
  - _Leverage: lib/api/coffee.ts (getCoffeeEvaluation), error handling patterns_
  - _Requirements: 3 (detail view), authorization check_
  - _Prompt: Role: Backend Developer with Next.js and security expertise | Task: Create Server Component container that fetches single evaluation by ID using getCoffeeEvaluation, handles 404 (not found) and 403 (unauthorized) with notFound() and error boundaries, checking user authorization to view | Restrictions: Must verify evaluation exists and user has access (own evaluation or public), use Next.js notFound() for 404, throw error for 403, handle Supabase errors gracefully | Success: Evaluation fetched correctly by ID, 404 handled with notFound(), authorization checked properly, errors are user-friendly_

- [ ] 3.5. Create detail page view (Presentational Component)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/[id]/_components/evaluation/view.tsx
  - Display all evaluation fields with ratings visualization
  - Show edit/delete buttons for owner
  - Purpose: Display complete evaluation details
  - _Leverage: RatingStars component, frontend-design styling, user session check_
  - _Requirements: 3 (detail view), 4 (edit button), 5 (delete button)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Frontend Developer with expertise in detail views and conditional rendering | Task: Create EvaluationDetailView component displaying all evaluation fields (shop, bean, roast, ratings with RatingStars, dates) with coffee theme styling, conditionally showing Edit/Delete buttons if user owns evaluation | Restrictions: Must be Server Component receiving evaluation and session data, use RatingStars for all 4 ratings, apply frontend-design styling, buttons only visible to owner, ensure accessible layout | Success: All evaluation data displays beautifully with proper formatting, ratings visualized with stars, Edit/Delete buttons show only for owner, layout is accessible and matches design_

- [ ] 3.6. Create detail page with delete action
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/[id]/page.tsx
  - Compose detail container and view
  - Add delete confirmation and action handling
  - Purpose: Main entry point for evaluation detail view
  - _Leverage: EvaluationContainer, deleteCoffeeEvaluation Server Action_
  - _Requirements: 3 (detail view), 5 (delete with confirmation)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Full-stack Developer with Next.js and UX expertise | Task: Create detail page composing container and view, implementing delete functionality with client-side confirmation dialog before calling deleteCoffeeEvaluation Server Action, with proper error handling and loading states | Restrictions: Must confirm before delete (use window.confirm or custom dialog), call Server Action properly, show loading state during deletion, redirect to list on success, display errors to user | Success: Page renders detail correctly, delete requires confirmation, loading states clear, successful deletion redirects to list, errors shown without breaking UI_

## Phase 4: Create & Edit Forms

- [ ] 4.1. Create EvaluationForm component (Client Component)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/evaluation-form.tsx
  - Implement form with CoffeeSlider for ratings
  - Add client-side validation and Server Action integration
  - Handle both create and edit modes via initialData prop
  - Purpose: Reusable form component for creating/editing evaluations
  - _Leverage: CoffeeSlider, components/ui/Button, components/ui/Input, Server Actions, useTransition_
  - _Requirements: 1 (create form), 4 (edit form), validation_
  - _Prompt: Role: React Developer with forms and Server Actions expertise | Task: Create EvaluationForm Client Component supporting both create (no initialData) and edit (with initialData) modes, using CoffeeSlider for 4 ratings, existing UI components for inputs, calling appropriate Server Action with FormData, using useTransition for loading states and displaying errors | Restrictions: Must be Client Component ('use client'), validate inputs before submission (required fields, 1-10 range), use progressive enhancement (works without JS via Server Actions), handle both create and update actions, show loading and error states clearly | Success: Form works in both create/edit modes, validation prevents invalid submissions, loading states during submission, errors displayed clearly, Server Actions called correctly, progressive enhancement works_

- [ ] 4.2. Create new evaluation page
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/new/page.tsx
  - Render EvaluationForm without initial data
  - Add page metadata
  - Purpose: Dedicated page for creating new evaluations
  - _Leverage: EvaluationForm component, metadata API_
  - _Requirements: 1 (evaluation creation)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Next.js Developer with App Router expertise | Task: Create new evaluation page that renders EvaluationForm component (no initialData prop for create mode), exports metadata with Japanese title/description, and serves as dedicated creation page route | Restrictions: Must be Server Component wrapping Client Component form, export proper metadata, minimal logic (just render form), ensure authenticated via middleware | Success: Page renders form in create mode, metadata correct, authentication enforced, form submission creates new evaluation_

- [ ] 4.3. Create edit evaluation page
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/[id]/edit/page.tsx
  - Fetch existing evaluation and pass to EvaluationForm
  - Verify user owns the evaluation
  - Purpose: Dedicated page for editing existing evaluations
  - _Leverage: lib/api/coffee.ts (getCoffeeEvaluation), EvaluationForm, authorization patterns_
  - _Requirements: 4 (evaluation edit), authorization_
  - _Prompt: Role: Full-stack Developer with security and Next.js expertise | Task: Create edit page that fetches evaluation by ID, verifies user ownership (throw 403 if not owner), passes evaluation as initialData to EvaluationForm, with proper error handling for not found and unauthorized | Restrictions: Must check user owns evaluation before showing form, use getCoffeeEvaluation for data, handle 404 with notFound(), handle 403 with error boundary, pass complete evaluation to form | Success: Page fetches correct evaluation, ownership verified, non-owners get 403 error, form pre-filled with existing data, updates work correctly_

## Phase 5: Search & Sort

- [ ] 5.1. Create SearchAndSort component (Client Component)
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/list/search-and-sort.tsx
  - Implement search input with debouncing
  - Add sort dropdown with options (date, rating, shop name)
  - Use URL search params for state management
  - Purpose: Provide search and sort functionality for list view
  - _Leverage: useSearchParams, useRouter, frontend-design search UI_
  - _Requirements: 6 (search functionality), 7 (sort functionality)_
  - _Prompt: Role: React Developer with URL state management expertise | Task: Create SearchAndSort Client Component with search input (debounced 300ms), sort dropdown, using Next.js useSearchParams for URL-based state management, triggering re-fetch via router.push with query params following frontend-design styling | Restrictions: Must be Client Component, use URL search params for persistence, debounce search input to avoid excessive requests, provide sort options (newest, oldest, rating high/low, shop name A-Z), maintain state on page refresh | Success: Search input debounced properly, sort dropdown works correctly, URL updates with search/sort params, state persists on refresh, UI matches frontend-design_

- [ ] 5.2. Update list container to handle search/sort params
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_containers/list/container.tsx (modify)
  - Read searchParams from page props
  - Pass to data fetching layer for filtering/sorting
  - Purpose: Enable server-side filtering and sorting
  - _Leverage: lib/api/coffee.ts (extend with search/sort), searchParams from page props_
  - _Requirements: 6 (search), 7 (sort)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Backend Developer with Next.js Server Components expertise | Task: Modify CoffeeListContainer to accept searchParams from page props, extract search query and sort option, pass to enhanced getCoffeeEvaluations function that filters and sorts data server-side using Supabase queries | Restrictions: Must read searchParams from props (Server Component pattern), perform filtering/sorting in database query (not client-side), handle empty/invalid params gracefully, maintain request memoization with cache() | Success: Search query filters results correctly (shop, bean, roast), sort options work as expected, database queries efficient with indexes, cached appropriately_

- [ ] 5.3. Integrate SearchAndSort into list page
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/page.tsx (modify)
  - Add SearchAndSort component above list view
  - Pass searchParams to container
  - Purpose: Complete search/sort integration
  - _Leverage: SearchAndSort component, searchParams prop_
  - _Requirements: 6 (search), 7 (sort)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Next.js Developer with composition expertise | Task: Integrate SearchAndSort component into main list page above CoffeeListView, accept searchParams in page component props and pass to CoffeeListContainer, ensuring URL-based state works end-to-end | Restrictions: Page must accept searchParams prop (Next.js App Router pattern), pass to container for server-side filtering, render SearchAndSort before list, handle loading states during search/sort changes | Success: SearchAndSort integrated visually above list, URL state works correctly, search/sort triggers re-fetch, loading states clear, user experience smooth_

## Phase 6: Profile Management

- [ ] 6.1. Create profile page with form
  - File: app/(app)/profile/page.tsx
  - Fetch user profile and render edit form
  - Implement profile update Server Action
  - Purpose: Allow users to manage their display name and bio
  - _Leverage: lib/supabase/server.ts, Server Actions pattern, form components_
  - _Requirements: 9 (user profile management)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Full-stack Developer with Supabase and forms expertise | Task: Create profile page that fetches current user's profile from user_profiles table, renders form with display_name and bio fields, implements updateProfile Server Action for updates, with proper validation and error handling | Restrictions: Must fetch authenticated user's profile, allow nullable display_name and bio (optional fields), validate max lengths (display_name: 100 chars, bio: 500 chars), use Server Action for mutation, show success message on update | Success: Profile fetches for authenticated user, form pre-filled with current data, updates save correctly, validation prevents invalid data, success/error messages clear_

## Phase 7: Testing & Polish

- [ ] 7.1. Create unit tests for data layer
  - File: lib/__tests__/api/coffee.test.ts
  - Test getCoffeeEvaluations, getCoffeeEvaluation, search functions
  - Mock Supabase client responses
  - Purpose: Ensure data fetching layer reliability
  - _Leverage: Jest, Supabase mocks, existing test patterns_
  - _Requirements: All data fetching requirements (2, 3, 6)_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with Jest and TypeScript testing expertise | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for lib/api/coffee.ts functions, mocking Supabase client to test success and error scenarios, verifying request memoization with cache(), ensuring proper error handling and type safety | Restrictions: Must mock Supabase client completely, test both success and error paths, verify cache() behavior, do not hit real database, maintain test isolation | Success: All data functions tested with good coverage, mocks work correctly, cache behavior verified, error handling tested, tests run fast and reliably_

- [ ] 7.2. Create unit tests for Server Actions
  - File: lib/__tests__/actions/coffee.test.ts
  - Test CRUD Server Actions with mocked Supabase
  - Verify revalidatePath and redirect calls
  - Purpose: Ensure mutation layer reliability and error handling
  - _Leverage: Jest, Supabase mocks, Next.js mocks (redirect, revalidatePath)_
  - _Requirements: All mutation requirements (1, 4, 5)_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with Server Actions testing expertise | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for lib/actions/coffee.ts Server Actions, mocking Supabase and Next.js utilities (redirect, revalidatePath), testing FormData parsing, validation, error handling, and cache invalidation | Restrictions: Must mock all external dependencies, test FormData input parsing, verify revalidatePath called before redirect, test validation errors returned correctly, do not hit real database | Success: All Server Actions tested thoroughly, FormData handling verified, errors returned properly to client, revalidatePath/redirect logic correct, tests reliable_

- [ ] 7.3. Create component unit tests
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/_components/__tests__/
  - Test CoffeeSlider, RatingStars, CoffeeCard, EvaluationForm
  - Use React Testing Library
  - Purpose: Ensure UI component reliability and accessibility
  - _Leverage: React Testing Library, Jest, existing component test patterns_
  - _Requirements: Component functionality (all UI requirements)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Frontend QA Engineer with React Testing Library expertise | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for all UI components (CoffeeSlider, RatingStars, CoffeeCard, EvaluationForm) using React Testing Library, testing user interactions, accessibility, and edge cases with proper mocking of Server Actions and router | Restrictions: Must test user interactions (clicks, keyboard, form submission), verify accessibility features (ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation), mock Next.js router and Server Actions, test edge cases and error states, follow testing-library best practices | Success: All components tested with good coverage, user interactions work correctly, accessibility verified, edge cases handled, tests are maintainable and readable_

- [ ] 7.4. Create integration tests for page flows
  - File: app/(app)/coffee/__tests__/integration/
  - Test complete user flows (create → list → detail → edit → delete)
  - Use MSW for API mocking
  - Purpose: Verify end-to-end functionality of coffee evaluation features
  - _Leverage: React Testing Library, MSW, Next.js testing patterns_
  - _Requirements: All functional requirements_
  - _Prompt: Role: Integration Test Engineer with Next.js and MSW expertise | Task: Write integration tests covering complete user journeys (creating evaluation, viewing list, opening detail, editing, deleting) using React Testing Library with MSW to mock Supabase API responses, verifying page navigation and data flow | Restrictions: Must mock Supabase API with MSW, test realistic user journeys end-to-end, verify page transitions and data updates, do not test implementation details, ensure tests are deterministic | Success: All user journeys tested successfully, navigation works correctly, data flows through pages properly, tests are reliable and maintainable_

- [ ] 7.5. Add loading and error states
  - Files: app/(app)/coffee/loading.tsx, app/(app)/coffee/error.tsx, app/(app)/coffee/[id]/loading.tsx, app/(app)/coffee/[id]/error.tsx
  - Create loading skeletons matching card/detail layouts
  - Create error pages with retry and back navigation
  - Purpose: Improve user experience during loading and error scenarios
  - _Leverage: Next.js loading.tsx and error.tsx conventions, frontend-design styling_
  - _Requirements: Non-functional requirement (usability, error handling)_
  - _Prompt: Role: UX Engineer with Next.js App Router expertise | Task: Create loading.tsx files with skeleton loaders matching card and detail layouts using frontend-design styling, and error.tsx files with user-friendly error messages, retry buttons, and back navigation following Next.js error boundary patterns | Restrictions: Must use Next.js loading.tsx for Suspense boundaries, error.tsx must be Client Components with reset function, match design styling, provide helpful error messages in Japanese, include retry and navigation options | Success: Loading skeletons match actual layouts closely, appear smoothly during data fetching, error pages are user-friendly with clear messages and actions, UX is polished and professional_

- [ ] 7.6. Polish UI/UX and accessibility
  - Files: All component files
  - Review and improve accessibility (ARIA, keyboard navigation)
  - Add animations and transitions from frontend-design
  - Optimize responsive design
  - Purpose: Ensure production-ready quality and accessibility
  - _Leverage: Frontend-design animations, WCAG guidelines, Tailwind utilities_
  - _Requirements: Non-functional requirements (accessibility, responsive design, animations)_
  - _Prompt: Role: Senior Frontend Developer with accessibility and UX expertise | Task: Review all components for accessibility (ARIA attributes, semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, color contrast), implement animations from frontend-design (fade-in, slide-up, stagger), optimize responsive design across all breakpoints, ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance | Restrictions: Must achieve WCAG 2.1 AA compliance minimum, test keyboard navigation thoroughly, ensure animations are performant (60fps), verify responsive design on mobile/tablet/desktop, maintain design consistency | Success: All components fully accessible and keyboard-navigable, animations smooth and performant, responsive design works perfectly across all devices, passes accessibility audits_

- [ ] 7.7. Add navigation links to layout
  - File: app/(app)/layout.tsx (modify)
  - Add "Coffee" navigation link to header/sidebar
  - Add "New Evaluation" quick action button
  - Purpose: Integrate coffee evaluation feature into main app navigation
  - _Leverage: Existing layout components, navigation patterns_
  - _Requirements: Integration with existing app_
  - _Prompt: Role: Frontend Developer with navigation and layout expertise | Task: Modify app layout to add "Coffee" navigation link to main menu and "New Evaluation" quick action button in header, following existing navigation patterns and ensuring active state highlights correctly on coffee pages | Restrictions: Must follow existing layout structure, use same styling patterns as other nav items, ensure active state works with Next.js pathname matching, maintain responsive behavior, test navigation on all pages | Success: Coffee link appears in navigation with proper styling, active state highlights on coffee pages, New Evaluation button easily accessible, navigation responsive on mobile, integration seamless with existing layout_

- [ ] 7.8. Final review and documentation
  - Files: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (if needed)
  - Document coffee evaluation feature usage
  - Add screenshots or demo GIFs
  - Create migration guide for database setup
  - Purpose: Ensure feature is well-documented for users and developers
  - _Leverage: Existing documentation patterns_
  - _Requirements: All_
  - _Prompt: Role: Technical Writer with software documentation expertise | Task: Document coffee evaluation feature in README.md including user guide (how to create/edit/search evaluations), developer guide (architecture, file structure, patterns), database setup instructions (running migrations), and add screenshots/GIFs showing feature in action | Restrictions: Must follow existing documentation style, include clear setup instructions for local development, document all user-facing features, provide architecture overview with diagrams, ensure documentation is beginner-friendly | Success: Documentation complete and clear, setup instructions work for new developers, user guide helpful for end users, architecture overview aids understanding, screenshots illustrate features effectively_
